title: Eventual Withdrawal (No Permanent Freeze of User Funds)

swc: SWC-128 DoS with block gas limit

descriptions.semantic: Any principal who has deposited recoverable funds and who satisfies the (statically known, finitely achievable) withdrawal precondition will, after submitting a well-formed withdrawal request, eventually receive those funds — under explicitly stated fairness and environmental assumptions. There is no reachable state from which a legitimately-entitled withdrawal is permanently unsatisfiable.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A progress property over the joint user-protocol-environment transition system: from every state in which a withdrawal is enabled, a fair scheduling of system steps reaches a state in which the withdrawal has completed. It is a reachability-under-fairness obligation on a non-terminating reactive system, not a single-transition constraint.
descriptions.security: Protects against value capture by indefinite denial of service: griefing, admin abuse (malicious or buggy pause that cannot be lifted), unbounded loops, dependency on a liveness-failed external actor (sequencer, oracle, relayer), or gas-exhaustion bricking. The failure mode is not theft but irrecoverable lock — economically equivalent to loss.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Manifests across many transactions and many blocks, possibly involving multiple actors. Violations are typically structural: a single point of liveness failure (one sequencer / one admin key / one oracle) with no permissionless fallback; an unbounded iteration whose gas cost grows with adversary-controlled state; a withdrawal path that can be front-run into permanent revert; a pause with no time bound or no forced-exit.
descriptions.formal_verification: A liveness property. It CANNOT be established by reachability/symbolic-execution tools that only search for reachable bad states — those prove safety. It requires (a) fairness assumptions to even be true, and (b) model checking with fairness (LTL/CTL with strong/weak fairness) or interactive proof of a well-founded ranking/variant function that strictly decreases toward completion. Bounded fuzzers cannot witness 'eventually'.

formalization.signature: Predicates over global state s: requested(u): user u has a pending valid withdrawal; entitled(u): u meets the withdrawal precondition; completed(u): u's funds transferred. Environment actions: chainStep (a block is produced), include(tx) (a submitted tx is sequenced).
formalization.first_order_logic: Well-foundedness witness:  exists rank: State -> Ordinal . forall s,s',u . ( requested(u) at s /\ ~completed(u) /\ s --> s' under a fair step ) -> ( completed(u) at s'  \/  rank(s') < rank(s) ).  Termination of the descending chain yields completion.

temporal_logic.ltl: G( (requested(u) /\ entitled(u)) -> F completed(u) )    -- 'request implies eventual completion'
temporal_logic.ctl: AG( (requested(u) /\ entitled(u)) -> AF completed(u) )   -- on ALL fair paths
temporal_logic.fairness:
REQUIRED, and load-bearing:
  (WF1) Weak fairness on chainStep: blocks are eventually produced (consensus liveness).
  (WF2) Strong fairness on include(tx): a continuously-resubmitted valid tx with sufficient fee is eventually sequenced (censorship resistance / forced inclusion).
  (A3) No unbounded adversarial growth of the work needed per withdrawal (bounded gas).
  Without WF1+WF2 the property is FALSE, not merely unproven.

formalization.state_machine: Büchi-style acceptance: the property is the set of infinite runs in which every 'requested & entitled' is eventually followed by 'completed'. The negation (a run with a request never satisfied) must be empty in the product of system x fairness constraints.
formalization.type_theoretic: Corresponds (Curry–Howard for temporal/linear logic) to a non-terminating process that is guaranteed to emit a 'completed' message on each open 'request' channel — a productivity/guardedness obligation in a coinductive setting. The variant function is the structural-recursion measure proving productivity.

relationships.note: In tension with unconditional Emergency-Pause-Safety: a pause that can freeze withdrawals indefinitely directly negates this guarantee. Resolution is a *bounded* or *forced-exit* pause, recorded as a refinement.
Relies on Consensus-Liveness (WF1) of the underlying chain.
Refined by L2-specific 'Escape-Hatch / Forced-Withdrawal' which removes the sequencer from the trust path.

attack_surface.pattern: withdrawal routed through one sequencer/relayer/oracle/admin with no permissionless fallback
attack_surface.notes: Most common structural cause; the fix is a fallback path enforced by WF2.

attack_surface.pattern: withdrawal iterates over an adversary-growable array; gas cost exceeds block limit
attack_surface.notes: Violates assumption A3; convert push to pull, cap iteration.

attack_surface.pattern: withdrawal does a low-level call to a contract that always reverts, bricking a batched payout loop
attack_surface.notes: Isolate each payee; favor pull over push.

attack_surface.pattern: guardian pause with no time bound and no forced-exit
attack_surface.notes: Direct conflict with BPO:0050; require timelocked auto-unpause or escape hatch.

metrics: max age of an open withdrawal request
count of requests open beyond SLA bound
invariant_checkpoints: no open request older than the protocol's stated bound N when forced-inclusion is available
runtime_assertions: liveness monitors are off-chain: a watcher asserting bounded completion latency; on-chain you can only assert the *enabling conditions* (e.g. escape hatch is reachable), not 'eventually' itself
telemetry: alert when any request exceeds the freeze-detection threshold

strategies.notes: Model the protocol + environment + WF1/WF2 fairness; check the LTL/CTL formula. Bounded by state-space size; abstraction needed for unbounded actor sets.
Discharge productivity via a well-founded measure that strictly decreases each fair step toward completion.
Cannot prove liveness; detects freeze empirically and triggers alerts/escape hatch.

testability: liveness is not unit-testable in the usual sense; test the ENABLING conditions: escape hatch reachable without sequencer; withdrawal bounded-gas; resubmission eventually included in a fairness-modeled harness

static: control-flow check that every freeze state has an exit edge
design_patterns: L2 forced-transaction queue (removes sequencer from liveness path)
no single mandatory third party on the exit path

assumptions.statement: Underlying chain produces blocks within bounded time (partial synchrony).
Consensus liveness holds (e.g. <1/3 or <1/2 adversarial depending on protocol).
User can pay inclusion fees and resubmit; mempool not perpetually censoring.
Per-withdrawal work is bounded independent of adversary-controlled state growth.

provenance.notes: The conflictsWith BPO:0050 edge is intentional and pedagogically central: unconditional liveness and unconditional emergency-pause safety are genuinely incompatible; real systems pick a *bounded* compromise, which BPO records as an explicit refinement rather than hiding the tension.
